CJI Kant himself today slammed the BCI's move. "Naturally, this is absolutely uncalled for. It’s a dialogue between students and me. Who are they to raise an issue? This is totally uncalled for. items.title: Karnataka Govt vs RSS: Cabinet clears Bill requiring permission for use of public property
items.summary: The Karnataka Cabinet has approved a Bill requiring organisations to obtain government permission before holding activities on public property. The Bill, approved on Thursday, August 13, comes amid a prolonged dispute between the Congress government and the RSS over the latter's use of public spaces. The Karnataka Regulation of Use of Government Premises and Public Property Bill, 2026, is expected to be introduced during the ongoing monsoon session of the legislature. The Bill has been drafted by the Home Department headed by Priyank Kharge. The proposed legislation will replace an October 18, 2025 government order that required private organisations, associations and groups to obtain prior permission to use government premises or public property. The order applied to private associations, societies, trusts, clubs and other bodies, whether registered or not, but was stayed by the Karnataka High Court on grounds including violation of fundamental rights. The earlier order had required organisations to seek permission at least three days before an event. items.title: Advocates acting as insolvency professionals liable to collect, deposit GST: Delhi High Court
items.summary: The Delhi High Court has ruled that advocates acting as insolvency professionals are liable to collect Goods and Services Tax (GST) from recipients of their services and deposit it with the government under the forward charge mechanism [Kanwal Chaudhary v. Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India]. A Division Bench of Justices Prathiba M Singh and Shail Jain held that advocates providing insolvency and receivership services must obtain GST registration and comply with the requirements applicable to insolvency professionals as a class. “ An Advocate acting as an Insolvency Professional would, therefore, be governed by the ‘forward charge mechanism’, which is applicable to Insolvency Professionals, as a class, and not by the ‘reverse charge mechanism’, which is otherwise applicable to Advocates rendering legal services ,” the Court said. Justice Prathiba Singh and Justice Shail Jain Under the forward charge mechanism, the service provider adds GST to the invoice, collects it from the recipient and deposits it with the government. Under reverse charge, the recipient of the service is responsible for depositing GST. The Court clarified that its ruling applies only to services rendered

items.title: Brand protection in the era of social commerce
items.summary: The rapid growth of social commerce has fundamentally altered how businesses build brands, engage consumers, and generate revenue. Social media platforms are no longer limited to communication and entertainment. They have evolved into sophisticated commercial ecosystems where businesses promote products, interact with consumers, complete transactions, and cultivate long term customer relationships. Platforms offering live shopping, influencer collaborations, short video marketing, and integrated purchasing features have transformed the commercial landscape across India. This evolution has created significant opportunities for businesses of every size. Startups, established enterprises, and independent entrepreneurs now reach national and international audiences without maintaining extensive physical retail infrastructure. Brand visibility has become easier to achieve than at any previous time.
